Patient Question: hi I experience excessive hair loss and patches all over my scalp that why I decided to shave my head I still have hair growing in my head but most of the parts are totally bald and base on the symthoms it is alopecia but I really dont know what it is!

Medical Response: Hello. Thanks for writing to us at Chat Doctor These bald areas are most likely patches of Alopecia Area ta(AA). Alopecia Area ta(AA) is an autoimmune condition. It usually presents as smooth bald patches of hair loss, most commonly over the scalp. The patches of Alopecia Area ta are smooth, and usually there is no evidence of inflammation like scaling or erythema or itching. Intra-lesional depot preparation of Triamcinolone acetone is the treatment of choice in adults. Patchy alopecia areas is a self limiting though new bald patches may appear, which may also need to be treated in the same way. Other topical treatments that have been tried either alone or in combination with intraluminal steroids are Topical Potent steroids (e. g. Mometasone Furnace, Clobetasol propionate); Topical Minoxidil solution; Topical Anthracite; Topical PVA(Morales +UVA therapy) etc would suggest you to visit a dermatologist for a confirmatory diagnosis as well as discussion regarding the most appropriate treatment for the bald patchesRegards
